about: Example answers from applications Kevin filled in correctly. 'rules' are answered straight away without the AI (they beat the built-in rules). 'applications' are worked examples the AI reads before it answers a form (the closest questions are sent with each page). 'notes' and 'ats' teach the AI how to work. Patterns are lower-case regular expressions; in 'pick', a value starting and ending with / is a pattern, anything else is the exact option. Profile values are written as {profile.key} and come from My info, so the street address and other private details never live in this file. To add an application: copy one block in 'applications', and add a line to 'rules' for any question that always has the same answer.
notes: Every REQUIRED field must be filled before pressing Next / Submit. Optional fields: fill them when the answer is known; never fill only part of an optional group (for example only the website of an optional 'Job 2'): either the whole group from the resume or none of it.

Technical-experience questions (do you have experience with X, describe a system you built, how do you use AI tools, testing, distributed systems): answer at once from the resume. Yes when the resume shows the skill (Node.js, TypeScript, Python, React, PostgreSQL, AWS, Azure, Kubernetes, Go and the others listed). Free text: 2-5 plain first-person sentences with real projects and numbers from the resume.

Salary / desired compensation: if the job shows a pay range, give its midpoint (a plain number such as 175000). If no range is shown, give a comfortable market figure for a senior engineer in that location, never a low number.
City is always Rancho Palos Verdes (not Rolling Hills). Location typeaheads: 'Rancho Palos Verdes, California, United States'.
Employer website in an employment-history section is the employer's own site (Jaburg & Wilk, P.C. -> https://www.jaburgwilk.com), never the candidate's portfolio.
Employment dates: follow the format the form shows (MM/YY to MM/YY -> 04/24 to 10/26). Dates come from the resume.

Education: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, California State University Dominguez Hills, from 2010 to 2014 (graduated 2014). Pick 'Bachelor's Degree' and 'Computer Science' from the offered options.

Location text boxes: 'Rancho Palos Verdes, CA' (or 'Rancho Palos Verdes, CA, USA' when the form shows a country). Some sites prefill Rolling Hills from the resume: replace it with Rancho Palos Verdes.
Salary asked as a range (base / OTE): give a range such as '$X - $Y' around the figure; with a posted range use that range. Salary with currency and period boxes: US Dollar, Yearly.

Answer the question that is asked. A question about the largest team managed needs team size and direct/indirect reports; a question about a recent hands-on issue needs one concrete incident. Never paste the answer of one box into another.
Never tick 'agree to receive text messages / SMS' boxes; tick the privacy / data-processing consent the application needs.
Never click 'Apply with LinkedIn', 'Apply with Indeed', 'Use My Indeed Resume' or 'Sign in with LinkedIn/Google'; upload the resume file instead.
Captchas (drag-the-piece puzzles, 'I am not a robot') are left to Kevin: stop and wait.

ats.name: Workday
ats.flow: Create an account on the company's Workday site (email + {{password}}) or sign in -> Autofill with Resume -> My Information (How did you hear: Indeed; previously employed: No; name, address, phone device type Personal Cell, country phone code United States of America (+1)) -> My Experience (check the work history and education the resume filled in, add Languages: English, all proficiencies 4 - Advanced) -> Application Questions -> Voluntary Disclosures (veteran, gender, ethnicity, terms checkbox) -> Self Identify (name, today's date, disability: No) -> Review -> Submit. Press 'Save and Continue' after each step. Leave Employee ID empty.

ats.name: Ashby
ats.flow: One page under the 'Application' tab. 'Autofill from resume' uploads the resume and fills name, email and location; then answer the questions top to bottom (Yes/No buttons are radio choices), fill the employment-history block for every required job, and press Submit Application.

ats.name: Jobvite
ats.flow: Add Resume (upload) -> Personal Information (first, last, preferred first name, email, home phone, address, city, state, zip) -> Desired Compensation -> Additional Files: upload the cover letter -> Next -> further pages of questions -> Submit. Skip 'Apply With LinkedIn'.

ats.name: Greenhouse
ats.flow: One page: first, last, email, country +1 and phone, Resume/CV Attach, Education (school, degree, discipline) dropdowns, the company's questions, Website and LinkedIn, then Voluntary Self-Identification (gender, Hispanic/Latino, race, veteran, disability) -> Submit application.

ats.name: SmartRecruiters
ats.flow: One page 'Easy Apply': skip 'Apply With Indeed'; Personal information (first, last, email, confirm email, Country/Region United States, City Rancho Palos Verdes, phone +1), Your Profiles (LinkedIn, Website; Facebook and X left empty), Resume (upload the tailored PDF), Message to the Hiring Team (the cover letter text), tick the privacy notice box -> Submit.

ats.name: Lever
ats.flow: One page: skip 'Apply with LinkedIn'; Resume/CV upload, Full name, Email, Phone, Current location, Current company, Links (LinkedIn, GitHub, Portfolio), the company's questions (Yes/No dropdowns and radios, free text), U.S. EEO (Gender, Race, Veteran) -> Submit Application.

qa.q: Please briefly describe a recent example where you personally worked on or troubleshot a production infrastructure issue involving cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, CI/CD, or Infrastructure as Code.
qa.a: At Jaburg & Wilk, our Airflow pipelines on Kubernetes started failing during peak loads. I traced it through pod logs and database metrics to parallel tasks exhausting PostgreSQL's connection limit, and fixed it with PgBouncer connection pooling and capped concurrency, while also rebuilding our CD pipeline with signed, Trivy-scanned images and smoke-tested deploys.

qa.q: Briefly describe your experience leading incident management for critical production systems, including Sev1/Sev2 incidents, postmortems, SLOs/SLIs, or reliability improvements.
qa.a: I've owned production reliability for critical legal and government systems, leading issues from triage through root-cause fix and follow-up: PgBouncer pooling for database connection exhaustion, retries and failure alerts on Airflow pipelines, OCR provider fallback with per-provider accuracy tracking, and smoke-tested, signed Kubernetes deploys to cut release risk. I haven't run a formal Sev1/Sev2 incident command process or defined SLOs and error budgets in a dedicated SRE team, but I've applied the same principles in practice and am ready to formalize them.
